newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares leap 2.7 pct ahead of votes.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares leap 2.7 pct ahead of votes.

text.p: Istanbul shares jumped in selective buys on Tuesday amid positive expectations that parliamentary probe votes to take place in parliament this evening would not hurt the government, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed 42 points, or 2.7 percent higher at a day's high of 1,596. Daily volume rose sharply to 27.44 trillion lira ($226.6 million) from Monday's 18.87 trillion ($156.2 million).

Brokers said there was brief selling at the start of the afternoon session due to the resignation of a deputy from the conservative coalition partner True Path Party (DYP) ahead of the votes, but buying resumed quickly afterwards.

"Buying strengthened after sales prompted at the start of the (second) session by the resignation of a deputy from the DYP. The thought that the parliamentary vote results will be positive dominated the market," said Yesim Cambazoglu from Alfa securities.

Parliament began the corruption debate to decide whether to send deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller to the Supreme Court on two corruption allegations dating from her three-year term as premier. Another corruption probe against Ciller will be debated on Wednesday.
Brokers said the market was likely to remain cautious due to two censure motions filed by leftist parties against the Islamist-led goverment, scheduled to be taken up in parliament on February 25.
"The parliamentary votes and motions are negatively affecting sentiment. The index is unlikely to pierce the 1,600 resistance even though it tried," sid Koray Cervatoglu from Baran securities.
